framework.name: UK NIS Regulations 2018 (SI 2018/506)
framework.description: The Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018 (SI 2018/506) — UK cybersecurity obligations for operators of essential services (OES) and relevant digital service providers (RDSP). Pending update by the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill (2025–2026).

objects.title: Security of network and information systems
objects.description: Operators of essential services must take appropriate and proportionate technical and organisational measures to manage risks to the security of network and information systems used to provide essential services.

objects.title: Incident prevention and minimisation of impact
objects.description: Measures must ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk posed and prevent and minimise the impact of incidents on the network and information systems used to provide an essential service.

objects.title: Incident notification — OES
objects.description: Operators of essential services must notify the relevant competent authority of any incident which has a significant impact on the continuity of the essential service provided, without undue delay.

objects.title: Security of digital services — RDSP
objects.description: Relevant digital service providers must identify and take appropriate and proportionate technical and organisational measures to manage security risks to their network and information systems.

objects.title: Incident notification — RDSP
objects.description: Relevant digital service providers must notify the relevant competent authority of any incident with a substantial impact on provision of the digital service.

objects.title: Governance — Managing security risk
objects.description: NCSC CAF Objective A: The organisation has appropriate management policies and processes in place to govern their approach to the security of network and information systems. Board-level ownership of security risk.

objects.title: Risk management
objects.description: NCSC CAF Objective A: The organisation identifies, assesses, and understands the risks to the security of networks and information systems supporting essential/digital services. Risk management is embedded in organisational processes.

objects.title: Protecting against cyber attack
objects.description: NCSC CAF Objective B: The organisation protects its network and information systems against cyber attack. Covers: service protection policies, identity and access control, data security, system security, resilient networks and systems, staff awareness and training.

objects.title: Detecting cyber security events
objects.description: NCSC CAF Objective C: The organisation detects cyber security events affecting, or with the potential to affect, essential services. Covers: security monitoring and anomaly detection; event discovery and reporting.

objects.title: Minimising the impact of cyber security incidents
objects.description: NCSC CAF Objective D: The organisation minimises the impact of cyber security incidents on the delivery of essential services. Covers: response and recovery planning, lessons learned, and civil emergency preparedness.

objects.title: Designation of competent authorities
objects.description: UK-sector competent authorities under NIS: NCSC/DSIT (digital), Ofcom (telecoms), FCA (financial infrastructure), NHSE (health), Environment Agency (water), BEIS (energy).

objects.title: Forthcoming: Cyber Security and Resilience Bill (2025–2026)
objects.description: The Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, introduced November 2025 and pending Royal Assent, will expand the scope of SI 2018/506 to cover more sectors, introduce mandatory incident reporting timelines, and strengthen enforcement powers. Organisations should monitor progress and prepare for updated obligations.

objects.title: Enforcement — penalties
objects.description: The competent authority may issue improvement notices and financial penalty notices. Maximum financial penalty: £17 million for OES; up to £8.5 million or 2% of global annual turnover for RDSP (whichever is higher).
